relevance_note: Case report of one woman with genetically confirmed adult-onset Alexander disease: 'AOAD was confirmed genetically with a positive glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) mutation'.
method_note: Single case report with no tables; built by a short script from my own reading; every span checked verbatim by script. In scope: the patient, plus four relatives described in relation to her: her mother (unsteadiness), her mother's mother and the mother's sister (wheelchair users due to unsteadiness), and a maternal uncle's son (affected by unsteadiness; diagnosed with Alexander's disease on a positive GFAP mutation). I assumed 'A maternal uncle's son' (case presentation) and 'her uncle's son' (diagnosis) are the same person. The paper writes 'her mother's mother and sister'; I read 'sister' as the mother's sister and labelled her 'mother's sister of patient'. The maternal uncle himself is not described as affected or tested and gets no row. No variant description is printed for either GFAP carrier, so both variant rows have variant_original_string 'not reported'; inheritance not reported (no parental testing). Age 60 is the age at presentation (used as age at last evaluation); the patient was followed up later at an unstated age. Onset age is not stated (only 'a 6-year history'), so left not reported. Vital status 'alive' rests on the present-tense follow-up sentence. n_patients_reported = 1 from 'This report describes a case'; the paper also mentions the cousin's GFAP-positive diagnosis. Relatives' 'unsteadiness' was not mapped to the ataxia checklist item (left not reported). 'Cognition was normal' recorded as cognitive impairment excluded (D-27) and cognitive decline excluded on the checklist. 'No pyramidal signs' recorded as spasticity or pyramidal signs excluded. 'The rest of the cranial nerves were normal' is a whole-examination statement; recorded as written and excludes nothing more specific. Dentate T2 hyperintensity was not counted as basal ganglia or thalamic abnormality. No contradictions found.

treatment_summary.value: clonazepam not tolerated; poor response to gabapentin, levetiracetam and memantine; CPAP not tolerated; variable positive pressure device triggered by breathing, adjusted by laryngoscopy to an inspiratory pressure level, gave significant relief of breathlessness at night and is increasingly used in the daytime
span: The patient unfortunately could not tolerate clonazepam and had a poor response to gabapentin, levetiracetam and memantine.
a standard continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) mask for sleep apnoea was not tolerated and a variable positive pressure device triggered by breathing was not helpful

it was subsequently possible using laryngoscopy to adjust the latter device to a pressure level during inspiration that minimised vocal cord closures associated with palatal tremor, and this provided significant relief of her breathlessness at night
she is increasingly using the variable positive pressure device during the daytime to relieve breathlessness
a clinical diagnosis of AOAD was made
AOAD was confirmed genetically with a positive glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) mutation

clinical_diagnosis_basis.value: both: clinical diagnosis of AOAD (progressive ataxia, dysarthria, eye movement abnormalities, palatal and tongue tremor, family history suggestive of autosomal-dominant inheritance), then positive GFAP genetic testing
span: In view of the progressive ataxia, dysarthria, eye movement abnormalities, palatal and tongue tremor and family history suggestive of autosomal-dominant inheritance, a clinical diagnosis of AOAD was made
subsequent GFAP genetic testing in our patient was positive
AOAD was confirmed genetically with a positive glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) mutation
